info.title: AquaPulse API
info.description:
Smart water management: buildings, homes, residents, live readings, water use, valve and pump control, tariffs, bills and payments, alerts and notifications, and the audit log.

Click **Authorize** and log in with a demo account (see `make seed`).

get.description: Alive: the API process answers.
Ready: the database and the MQTT broker can be reached. 503 if not.

post.description: Email + password → a 15-minute access token and a 7-day refresh token.

Same as /login, as an HTML form. Used by Swagger's **Authorize** button
(type your email in the *username* box; with two-factor login on, put the
6-digit code in the *client_secret* box).
Swap a refresh token for new tokens. Each refresh token works **once**.
End this session: its refresh token stops working, and so do its access tokens.
End every session of this account (all phones and browsers).
Email a reset link. The answer is the same whether or not the account exists.
Set a new password with the emailed code (works once, for 30 minutes).

A resident joins their home with the emailed invitation code (works once, 48 h).

New residents choose a password here. Someone who already has an account
(e.g. moving to another flat) types their existing password instead.

get.description: Who am I? Includes my buildings (owner) or my current home(s) (resident).

post.description: Change my password. Every other session is logged out, this one too: log in again.
Step 1: a new secret for the authenticator app. Nothing changes until step 2.
Step 2: type the code the app shows. Returns 10 recovery codes, shown only now.
10 new recovery codes (the old ones stop working). Needs password and code.
Switch two-factor login off. Needs the password and a current code.

get.description:
Download everything AquaPulse keeps about me: profile, homes, bills,
payments and daily water use (FR-75).

200.description: My data, as a JSON file

post.description:
Delete my account (residents). My name, email and phone are removed for
good and I am logged out everywhere. Bills keep their amounts, under
"Deleted resident", because the building's accounts must still add up.
Owners and admins cannot delete themselves here: their buildings would
have no one in charge.

get.description:
Red or green for the database, the MQTT broker, the ingestor and the
worker, plus devices online, readings per minute, refused messages, failed
emails and the last audit check (FR-55, FR-31).

schema.title: Response List Owners Api V1 Admin Owners Get

post.description: Create a building owner account with a first password (they can change it).

patch.description: Rename, disable or re-enable an owner. Disabling logs them out everywhere.

get.description: The whole audit log, newest first, with filters.

schema.title: Response All Audit Api V1 Admin Audit Get

post.description:
Re-calculate every hash now: proves no audit entry was changed or removed.
The worker also does this every day; GET /admin/audit/checks lists the results.

get.description: The latest audit chain checks, newest first (daily and on demand).

schema.title: Response Audit Checks Api V1 Admin Audit Checks Get

get.description: Emails by status, newest first. "failed" = not delivered after 3 retries (FR-60).

schema.title: Response Notifications Api V1 Admin Notifications Get
Response List Buildings Api V1 Buildings Get

post.description: Owners create buildings for themselves; a System Admin must say which owner.

patch.description:
Edit name, address, time zone, currency, due days and the billing settings.
The currency is fixed once bills exist. Only a System Admin can move a
building to another owner.

get.description: Audit entries about this building and its homes, newest first (FR-28).

schema.title: Response Building Audit Api V1 Buildings  Building Id  Audit Get
Response List Homes Api V1 Buildings  Building Id  Homes Get

get.description: Owners and admins see any home they manage; residents only the home they live in.

delete.description: Archive a home (soft delete). Nothing is erased, so billing history stays (FR-20).

post.description: Email a one-time code (valid 48 h) that lets the resident join this home.

get.description: Who lived here and when (newest first), with their name and email.

schema.title: Response List Occupancies Api V1 Homes  Home Id  Occupancies Get

patch.description: Set a move-out date, or choose the billing contact.

get.description: Latest reading, the valve state the device reported, and any lock.

Raw readings, oldest first: at most 7 days per call (default: the last hour).
With `every`, one averaged reading per period instead (a 7-day chart needs
a few hundred points, not 60,000).

parameters.name: every

schema.description: Average per this many seconds (for charts)
schema.title: Every

parameters.description: Average per this many seconds (for charts)

schema.title: Response Home Telemetry Api V1 Homes  Home Id  Telemetry Get

get.description: Litres per hour, day or month, in the building's time zone (FR-23).
All homes together per hour, day or month, plus the total of each home.

post.description: Open or close the home's water valve. Returns the command (202 Accepted).

get.description: What became of a command (FR-24).

post.description:
Lock the valve open or closed, with a reason of 10+ characters (FR-27).

The valve is moved to the locked position at once, and the residents
are told by email. Nobody can change it until the lock is removed.
Remove the lock, with a reason of 10+ characters. The valve stays where it is.

get.description: Live tank level, pump state, confirmed settings and commands still running.
Tank level over time, and pump hours and energy per day (FR-26).

patch.description:
Change thresholds, auto/manual mode or the pump's power (kW).

Thresholds and mode are sent to the device (202): the values shown change
once the device confirms them. The pump's kW is only used for the energy
estimate, so it is saved at once.

post.description:
Switch the pump on or off by hand (the tank must be in manual mode).

The device has the last word: it refuses `on` when the sump is empty
(UNSAFE_DRY_RUN) or the tank is full (UNSAFE_OVERFLOW), and the command
then ends as `rejected` with that reason.

get.description: Every device of the building, revoked ones included.

schema.title: Response List Devices Api V1 Buildings  Building Id  Devices Get

post.description: Register the meter/valve node of a home. The password is shown only once.

409.description: There is already an active device here

post.description: Register the building's tank node. The password is shown only once.

409.description: There is already an active device here

post.description: Give the device a new password. The old one is refused within seconds.
Switch the device off for good: it is disconnected and can never log in again.
A one-time ticket to open the live WebSocket, valid for 30 seconds.

get.description: Every version, newest first.

schema.title: Response List Tariffs Api V1 Buildings  Building Id  Tariffs Get

post.description:
Save a new tariff version. Slabs must start at 0, follow each other
with no gap or overlap, and the last one has no upper limit (to_l null).
Rates are per 1,000 litres in the building's currency.

An example bill for a tariff that is not saved yet, calculated by the
same engine as real bills, so the preview always matches (FR-45).

Make the draft bills of a finished month (e.g. "2026-09") from the meter
readings. Safe to run again: drafts are recalculated, issued bills are kept.

get.description: The building's bills, newest month first, by unit.

schema.title: Response List Bills Api V1 Buildings  Building Id  Bills Get

post.description: Issue every draft of the month in one go (FR-45 criterion 3).

get.description: Your own bills, newest first (drafts are not shown until issued).

schema.title: Response My Bills Api V1 Me Bills Get

get.description:
Every bill that still has something to pay, oldest due date first, with
the totals per currency (FR-38). Owners: all their buildings, or one.
A bill with its lines and payments.
The bill as an A4 PDF (FR-36).

post.description: Issue a draft: it gets its number and due date, and the resident an email.

Cancel a bill, with a reason of 10+ characters. To correct it, generate the
month again: the new draft will say which bill it replaces.

Record cash, a bank transfer or another payment. Less than the amount due
makes the bill partially paid; more than it is refused.

Undo a payment recorded by mistake (it is kept, marked reversed). For a
Stripe payment, refund it in the Stripe dashboard too.

put.description: Attach a photo of the receipt (optional, FR-40).

post.description:
Warn the resident that the water may be closed for this overdue bill.
A shut-off (valve lock with bill_id) is allowed 48 hours later at the
earliest, and only if the building's policy allows it (FR-27).

Open a Stripe Checkout page (TEST mode, no real money) for what is still
to pay. The bill is marked paid only when Stripe's signed webhook arrives.

Called by Stripe (not by apps). Only a correctly SIGNED message counts;
the same message twice is recorded once.

get.description: Alerts you may see, newest first.

parameters.name: active

schema.description: true: open or acknowledged; false: closed
schema.title: Active

parameters.description: true: open or acknowledged; false: closed

schema.title: Response List Alerts Api V1 Alerts Get

post.description:
"I have seen it." Records who and when (FR-59 criterion 3). The alert
stays until it is resolved, or the problem is gone for 10 minutes.

Close an alert by hand, e.g. after fixing the problem. If the problem is
still there, the next reading opens a new alert.

get.description:
Every built-in rule: on or off, its numbers and their safe limits, and
who gets an email for each severity.

patch.description:
Switch rules on or off and change their numbers, within safe limits.
Only what you send changes (to go back to a default, send the default
value). Audited. The worker uses the new settings within 10 seconds.

Which alerts also come by email and by push (FR-52): this severity and
above (or "off"), alert types never sent that way, and quiet hours when
non-critical emails and pushes wait. In-app alerts are always on. Takes
effect for the next alert.

post.description:
The Android app sends its Firebase token after login (and when Firebase
gives it a new one). A token belongs to one person: if someone else logs
in on the same phone, it moves to them.
Logging out in the app: no more pushes to this phone.

get.description:
This home's litres in a month, last month, and the building average per
person (only with 3 or more occupied homes). Months not over yet count until today.

What this month's water costs so far, with the building's real tariff.
Not a bill: the real one is made after the month ends (FR-35).
Everything the building dashboard and the homes list show, in one answer.

Litres per home per day, bills by month, or payments by day received,
for at most 400 days.

One home's litres per day, or its bills. A resident gets only their
own stay and their own bills.

Leak and burst findings of the last `days` days, newest first, each with
a plain-language reason and the readings behind it.

schema.title: Response Home Insights Api V1 Homes  Home Id  Insights Get

get.description:
The next 7 days of litres with an 80% range, and the month-end total and
bill estimate, made with the building's real tariff (FR-65). Residents:
from their move-in day only.

The whole building: total litres forecast, and the sum of every home's
month-end bill estimate.
Every trained version, newest first, with its scores and whether it is live.
